anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, the isolated CAN transceivers U11 and U10 have both of their isolated ground pins connected to the same global GND: U11.GND1 (pin 4) and U11.GND2 (pin 5) are tied to GND, and U10.GND1 (pin 4) and U10.GND2 (pin 5) are also tied to GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes two isolated CAN buses using an isolated CAN transceiver. An isolated CAN transceiver requires the primary-side and secondary-side grounds to remain separate (e.g. GND and an isolated CAN ground) so that galvanic isolation is preserved.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U11 pins GND1 and GND2 are both connected to GND; U10 pins GND1 and GND2 are both connected to GND.
Motor/actuator interfaces: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The intended galvanic isolation of the CAN buses is defeated, creating ground loops and removing the isolation/protection that the isolated CAN transceiver topology was intended to provide for the motor/actuator interfaces.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows a deviation in the CAN isolation architecture: the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have their isolated grounds tied together to GND, which contradicts the specified isolated CAN bus design.
